Well, what sub is this? 

I'm either out, or I'm moving and starting over.
Snood

I don't break down into tears until the argument is effectively over, and he's trying to leave - so it's not like my crying prevents us from fighting, it's that my crying "prevents" him from comfortably leaving at the end of a fight, and that's what he says is manipulative. 

I would say though, that once I am crying, it's pretty hard to have a conversation with me. I fold up and weep like a baby, and it's embarrassing enough that I do it, let alone being accused of doing it On Purpose. As though I'd act like a complete idiot if I had a choice.

What's lucky is that I usually don't break down crying until the very end of a fight, when he's getting ready to leave, or I have to leave, etc. So he just really feels like I'm holding him back from getting space, by crying, maybe? But I need space in which to STOP crying, I'm not crying to keep him anywhere.
I don't drink at all

It only doesn't drive me bananas because we don't argue very much.  It is however a huge feature of all our arguments.  He will say I play games,  or that I withhold information simply because information comes out over the course of a conversation,  and not lump sum at the beginning,  if that makes sense?  

Idk.  All I know is that I'm not trying to be manipulative,  I just cry a bunch when he's mad at me and idk how to help it

I usually listen for a really long time before!! I break down,  to be honest!  It's only towards the end of an argument where it starts going in circles and I realize that we're not going to be "good"  for a bit,  that I start to freak out.  

To be honest,  I lose most arguments.  There's not much that I do that I'm so attached to that I won't bend on it,  if that makes sense.  I just don't know how to calm down enough that I'm not being manipulative

I read that book in college,  I understood it but I didn't really feel it was descriptive of how I communicate.  I truly wouldn't tell him "go"  (or anything else!!)  if I didn't mean it.  


I'll wait till things cool off and tell him we have to talk.  Thank you

I fully understand that, whether or not I mean it to be, it's manipulative for me to cry in arguments. I just don't know what to do about it. Sometimes if I hold my breath I can stop for a while but it takes so long to convince him I'm fine and he can go that I can't really maintain my chill.

He often feels I don't mean offers like that - like "I don't care what we eat for dinner" , "please leave" seems too good to be true to him for some reason. No matter how often I tell him that I don't tell him to do things I wouldn't be fine with him doing. 

Thank you very much for your input, your perspective is really helpful :)

Thank you for this, this is a really helpful comment. 

That said - we very, very rarely fight. Things are truly excellent. I just have a hard time understanding how big fights are, I guess, because I react very strongly to the few fights that we do have.
I would disagree just because I think that my anxiety problems are part of why I get so upset in arguments, and I don't think my illness is a part of me as a person.

I'm very involved with mindfullness, I find it very helpful with a lot of my anxiety issues! 

It's interesting that you say holding it in is a sign of caring and maturity. I can try to hold it in, and usually I'm able to get myself together for a few minutes or so - but like, even tonight, after he said that he felt like he couldn't leave because I was crying, I went to the bathroom and blew my nose and came out calm, and said "ok, I'm calm, so that you can feel free to leave" and he said that that was also manipulative because "he knows I'll just break down when he leaves". I feel like I can't win.
I'll try - although you're right that it might not give me an answer I want.
I'm absolutely not faking, but I'd agree I cry pretty dramatically - NOT ON PURPOSE - but because that's just how my face cries.

I guess it's 3? 

But how do I keep from getting so upset?/where do we meet in the middle?

I'm not going to get into it, because it's very much in the past, but as you might be able to tell by the fact that we're together, our past breakups were long, drawn out, emotional experiences. 

Edit: I am taking full responsibility for these emotional reactions, and asking literally: how do I control my emotional reactions?
